title: Do the thinking before you prompt
principle: The best way to get output that matches your vision is to tell Claude what you need up front. Spend time writing prompts before you design—dictate in the tool, type in Notes, or record a voice note on a walk and paste the transcript later. Figure out what you want away from the computer so Claude can execute your exact vision when you sit down.
procedure: Step away from the canvas and decide what you actually want: goal, audience, constraints, and success criteria.
Capture the brief however you think best—voice dictation in Claude Design, a phone Notes draft, or a walk voice-note transcript.
Paste or speak the full brief into Claude Design before asking for visuals.
Only then iterate on the output; don’t use the first empty prompt as a substitute for intent.
examplePrompts:
Before designing anything: here is the full brief I wrote offline.

Goal: <what this artifact must communicate>
Audience: <who sees it>
Constraints: <brand, format, time, fidelity>
Must include: <flows, screens, or beats>
Must avoid: <defaults or aesthetics I do not want>

Execute this vision. Do not invent a different concept.
tips: Nate: “I spend a lot of time writing prompts before I design.”
Dictation, couch Notes drafts, and walk transcripts are all valid brief-capture methods he names.
Efficiency comes from front-loading intent, not from prompting blank and hoping.
